audit_result.proof_trace: No check in any code path (handle_liquidation L496-544, liquidation_inner L691-793, ensure_liquidate_borrow_allowed L927-982) prevents ctx.sender() from being the owner of the obligation being liquidated. The Obligation struct stores no owner address and the ObligationOwnerCap is not required by the liquidation call. The liquidation incentive (liquidation_incentive * (1 - liq_revenue_factor) > liq_revenue_factor for typical values) makes self-liquidation net-positive: the borrower pays D in debt tokens and receives collateral worth D*(1+incentive)*(1-fee), violating net_value(post) <= net_value(pre).
audit_result.attack_scenario: An underwater borrower calls liquidate_as_coin (via any whitelisted interface package with PackageCallerCap) passing their own obligation_id; they pay D debt tokens and receive seized collateral worth D*(1+incentive)*(1-fee), capturing the liquidation bonus that should incentivize third-party liquidators and effectively extracting value from the protocol reserves.
